description: The real P2.0 output: per-layer, per-input-channel activation statistics for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, collected over 128 C4 calibration samples. This is what P2.1's per-channel scaling calibration will consume.

sanity_checks.layer_count: 197 = 28 decoder layers x 7 Linear submodules (q/k/v/o_proj, gate/up/down_proj) + 1 lm_head -- matches Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct's known architecture
sanity_checks.q_k_v_proj_consistency: q_proj/k_proj/v_proj within the same decoder layer have byte-identical per-channel stats, as expected since they consume the same hidden_states input -- confirms the hook is reading INPUT, not output

notable_finding.description: Ranking layers by (max_abs across channels) / (average of mean_abs across channels) surfaces a small number of mlp.down_proj layers with extreme outlier ratios -- far above the typical ratio (~25-30x) seen in attention o_proj layers.
notable_finding.interpretation: This is the real-model manifestation of the exact phenomenon AWQ (and SmoothQuant/LLM.int8() before it) is built to handle: a small number of activation channels carry disproportionately large magnitude ('outlier channels'), concentrated in specific layers (mlp.down_proj here). Naively quantizing every channel with the same scale would let a handful of outlier channels dominate the quantization error budget. This is exactly the signal P2.1's per-channel scaling factors are meant to act on -- not a hypothetical from the paper, but something visibly present in this project's own calibration run.
notable_finding.caveat: This is a scalar summary ratio for eyeballing which layers deserve attention, not a claim about which SPECIFIC channels are salient -- that requires looking at the full per-channel vector (in the .pt file), which P2.1 will do directly.

next_step: P2.1 -- per-channel scaling factor calibration (AWQ's core algorithm). Estimated 3-4 days; the plan's own warning is that the hard part is the fake-quantize round->clamp->dequantize ORDER, not the scaling-factor math itself.
